entries:
Alpha 1.0.11 (grounded in the dungeon)

  • Ground spells respect solid walls: Gravity Well, Meteor Drop, Inferno Cataclysm and legacy Rain of Arrows reject blocked ground placement without spending mana or starting cooldowns. Reachable floor through an open doorway remains a valid target.
  • Area damage stays on reachable ground: These spells and persistent ground zones no longer damage enemies through solid dungeon walls. Gravity Well cannot pull enemies through them, and Meteor's shield-explosion combo respects the same boundary. Friendly Consecrated Ground healing and Sanctuary retain their existing rules.
  • Meteor scatter stays connected: Cluster and Apocalypse impacts stop at dungeon boundaries instead of scattering into a disconnected room. Each meteor's warning and impact use its corrected position.
  • Verification continues: Real Wizard controls now check blocked and accepted ground casts. The wider all-class, party, area-effect presentation and full-dungeon milestone remains open.

Alpha 1.0.10 (paths, not just landings)

  • Death recovery stays deliberate: Recall no longer leaves a dead character standing at zero health or predicts a false arrival in town. Use the death screen's Respawn button to recover in Lanternhold, then return through the Dungeon Guide.
  • Your unfinished run waits: The last party member recalling or respawning now starts the existing five-minute return window. Returning within that window keeps the dungeon's layout and encounter progress; a teammate staying inside keeps the run occupied.
  • Basic attacks respect dungeon walls: Attacks need a clear path both when they start and when they land. Moving behind a solid wall during the wind-up prevents the hit; open doorways stay valid, and old attacks cannot follow you into another instance.
  • Marks need a reachable enemy: Weak Point Mark, Mark of Weakness and legacy Smite reject invalid or wall-blocked targets without spending mana or starting cooldowns. Cursor-selected casts publish the actual enemy target for their effects. Arcane Missiles drops invalid homing targets while still allowing ordinary cursor-directed volleys.
  • Damage feedback stays in your instance: Basic-hit and reflected-damage events retain their dungeon identity instead of being broadcast to unrelated instances.
  • Movement respects dungeon walls: Charge, Shattering Charge, Teleport and jumping follow the full path through dungeon floors. Landing in another room no longer lets these moves skip a solid wall; open doorways remain passable.
  • Shadowsteps need a reachable target: Shadow Strike, Shadow Lunge and Backstab reject enemies behind solid dungeon walls before spending mana, starting cooldowns or applying damage and debuffs. Rogue blink landings also respect the intervening geometry.
  • Charge reaches its real landing: The client follows server-controlled dash steps and the final landing, even when the remaining distance is smaller than ordinary movement correction thresholds.
  • Rejected casts explain themselves: Server rejections now explain cooldowns, action locks, stuns, locked skills and invalid cast requirements while restoring authoritative mana and cooldown state.
  • Dungeon verification continues: Fresh Wizard and Fighter browser checks cover wall-bound movement, jumps, open-floor movement and recall. The broader five-dungeon, all-class and party milestone remains open.

Alpha 1.0.9 (walls hold, roads continue)

  • Projectiles respect dungeon walls: travelling fireballs, daggers, and other ground projectiles stop at the first solid boundary instead of crossing into another room. Their full travel segment is checked, including large simulation steps.
  • Doorways stay open: shared room and corridor edges remain passable. This uses the dungeon's authoritative floor geometry, not invisible extra blockers at every tile seam.
  • Wall impacts tell the truth: blocked projectiles show an impact at the wall without displaying a false explosion damage area. Explicit zero-radius impacts survive the network payload and client effect rendering.
  • Directions name the right town: Ilyra's opening objective and daily contract descriptions now name Lanternhold consistently. Existing quest acceptance and progress are preserved.
  • More of the dungeon journey is checked: full-run QA now supports regional dungeon choices, replay seeds, difficulty, completed-run recall and re-entry. Molten Core's five-boss Fighter route passes, and skill/rune damage checks cover all five dungeons. The broader four-class, party and campaign verification remains open for 1.1.

Alpha 1.0.8 (the last teammate standing)

  • A teammate can turn the round: 2v2 arena rounds end only when an entire team is eliminated. The survivor keeps fighting; duplicate deaths cannot add points. Arenas remain first to two round wins, with a short recovery interval between rounds.
  • Practice means practice: duels no longer award rating, honor, season points, or ranked wins and losses. Leaving a practice duel has no ranked queue penalty. Ranked arena rewards and its five-minute forfeit penalty remain unchanged.
  • Know when to wait: the arena panel shows remaining teammates and round recovery. Eliminated players receive PvP-specific guidance and an explicit Forfeit and Leave Match action instead of a misleading town respawn button.
  • Finish cleanly: town respawn and recall cannot bypass an active PvP match. Round and match recovery clear old movement targets, practice results reach both players, and finished matches no longer linger in the arena panel.

Alpha 1.0.7 (your bag, your adventure)

  • Quest materials have faces: Verdant Memory Seeds, Moon-Tide Pearls, Cinderheart Ore, and Stormglass Pinions now have distinct elemental bag icons with a gold quest mark. Future Chronicle materials also have a safe relic-icon fallback.
  • Drag items out to drop them: drag a regular bag item onto the game world and release to place its whole stack at your feet. Click the ground item to recover it; auto-loot will not immediately take back items you deliberately dropped. Ground loot follows the existing one-minute expiry, and other players can pick it up.
  • Your story materials stay safe: quest items cannot be dropped. The server also rejects changed bag slots, repeated drops, dead/disconnected characters, and drops during an active player trade. Dropped items preserve their stats, sockets, and stack.
  • Choose your tracked quests: open the Journal (J) and use Track on screen on the story chain or any accepted daily. Selections are remembered per character in this browser; story tracking follows the next chapter. Selected quests scroll within the left tracker instead of being cut off after the first three.

Alpha 1.0.6 (every road has an ending)

  • A complete route when generation fails: exhausting dungeon layout retries now builds a connected fallback with ordinary enemies, elites, and every required boss instead of leaving an empty starting room. Elemental raid fallbacks retain their defended crystal-repair event.
  • Required bosses are checked: new layouts must include their full boss sequence and actual boss spawns inside the correct rooms. Failed attempts are cleaned up before another layout or the fallback is populated.
  • Recover old empty fallbacks: restoring an old saved run containing only a fallback starting room repairs that unusable route. Valid saved layouts and cleared encounters remain unchanged.
  • Enemies keep their identity: ordinary and elite dungeon spawns no longer overwrite another enemy when random identifiers collide, keeping the world registry and spatial index consistent.
  • Fallbacks have their own checks: forced-failure tests cover all five dungeons and five raid layouts at each difficulty, with High/Low floor and collision checks. Full multi-class, party, campaign, and raid-event verification remain open for 1.1.

Alpha 1.0.5 (your party holds its ground)

  • Return without moving your party: continuing a saved dungeon or raid brings back only the returning player. Teammates already inside keep their position and progress, and repeated entry requests no longer reset movement.
  • The portal remembers the real run: Continue Party Run shows the saved dungeon, difficulty, and level. These settings stay locked until the leader resets an empty instance.
  • Restored runs stay active: logging back into a restored dungeon now cancels its empty-instance timer and restores your room summary instead of treating the occupied run as abandoned.
  • Access follows the adventure: returning players must qualify for the actual saved run, including its level and Chronicle requirements. Choosing an easier dungeon cannot bypass a higher-level dungeon or crystal/Dark Realm raid gate.
  • Start together, return individually: only leaders can start fresh dungeon runs, and the whole group is checked before launch. Qualified raid members can return to an existing formed raid individually; a new raid still requires its normal ready check.
  • Party recovery is tested through real controls: two-player checks cover member and leader recall/re-entry while preserving the teammate’s scene and the run’s seed. Full-dungeon, wipe, campaign, and wider ability verification remain open for 1.1.

Alpha 1.0.4 (roads that remember)

  • Dungeon combat keeps running after a room clear: removed a deadlock between room rewards and enemy movement that could freeze the world before the first boss fight. Room rewards remain reserved once, with combat and later rooms able to continue updating.
  • Water and darkness have room to move: removed an unrelated scene boundary from canonical dungeon collision. Abyssal Well, Umbral Nexus, and the crystal and Dark King raids now use their own walkable bounds instead of pushing valid positions toward the old edge. Dungeon walls remain enforced.
  • A clear way home: the Escape menu now has Return to Lanternhold (B), using the same recall action as the keyboard shortcut. Help and completed-dungeon guidance explain this route instead of telling you to backtrack to an exit.
  • Arrive without old momentum: entering a dungeon now clears jumps, charges, and targets from the scene you left, just as recall and respawn do. Cooldowns and buffs remain intact.
  • Continue after reconnecting: dungeon entry, reset, and other legacy menu actions now follow the active connection instead of silently sending to a closed socket. A real-server Water route checks movement, reconnect, town recall, and return to the same saved run.
  • Party leaders can safely reset: corrected the party identity check that hid Reset from the actual leader. Non-leaders remain unable to reset, and everyone must leave the instance before it can be cleared.
  • Dungeon reports can be replayed: regional layouts use independent seeds. Saved runs retain their geometry and record a precise seed and generator version, so unrelated combat or loot randomness cannot change a reproduced hallway.
  • Broader dungeon checks: production seed sweeps and real-coordinate floor/collision checks cover all five dungeons and the elemental and Dark King raid layouts. Full encounters, party recovery, and campaign progression remain part of the open 1.1 verification gate.

Alpha 1.0.3 (within reach, safely home)

  • Large bosses stay within melee reach: multiplayer actors now use the server's collision radius instead of decorative model bounds. Oversized bodies on bosses such as Rustbound Colossus and Hollow Sentinel no longer stop melee characters outside their attack range.
  • Leave dungeon movement behind: recall and respawn clear departed charge and jump destinations, height, and targets. Scene transitions also clear predicted movement and queued casts; delayed town or legacy dungeon loading cannot overwrite a newer instance.
  • Teleport stays in your realm: corrected an old coordinate clamp that displaced Wizard Teleport casts in Air, Fire, and dungeon instances. Overworld casts use the current realm boundaries, while dungeon destinations retain their walkable-area constraints.
  • Dungeon verification continues: these are targeted repairs, not a declaration that every dungeon issue is resolved. Full boss encounters, other abilities, party recovery, and randomized traversal remain release-blocking work for 1.1.

Alpha 1.0.2 (rewards and roads that meet)

  • Dungeon floors share one footprint: rooms, hallway bends, and crossings now render from the same walkable area the server uses. Floor partitions do not overlap, tiles keep a shared scale and alignment, and boundary walls no longer cut across connected passages.
  • Quest rewards worth collecting: story and daily turn-ins grant gold plus experience. At level 100, experience goes into the existing Resonance progression instead; overflow from reaching the cap does too. Offers, the Journal, and completion dialogue show the reward, including the exact XP/Resonance split received.
  • Spells reach every realm: fixed an old world-boundary check that immediately removed projectiles in the Air and Fire realms. Fireball and other projectile abilities can now travel and hit there.
  • A wizard needs your help: meet Archmage Ilyra in the open town square to accept the Chronicle. Each chapter now waits for you to return and click Complete Quest; rewards and the next chapter no longer arrive automatically. Fifteen authored turn-in conversations deepen the story of the four crystals and Malachar.
  • Follow the right marker: Ilyra has gold quest symbols and the daily quest giver has blue ones. An exclamation mark means quests are available; a question mark takes priority when you can turn one in. Quest givers are friendly interaction targets, never attack targets.
  • A tidier quest tracker: a compact, story-first shortlist keeps the HUD readable with many accepted quests. The full Journal is one click away, and the tracker leaves room for permanent chat on short and narrow screens. Opening the party roster compacts the tracker to its Journal shortcut so party controls stay visible and clickable.
  • Town walls match the buildings: the rotated trading house, stash coffer, and Oathhall behind it use current wall footprints instead of oversized old model and roof bounds. Removed service models also remove their collision shapes.
  • Spirit Guardians become cherubs: little rounded angels with bare torsos, curls, feathered wings, and halos orbit your Cleric. Animated wings and shared, batched geometry preserve the existing aura radius, runes, boosted guardian count, and server-owned damage.
  • Dungeon repair continues: reported return-to-town failures, boss attackability, and dungeon-specific ability problems remain under investigation. This patch does not claim those issues are resolved; they remain priorities before 1.1.
